proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating fluoride with a fully reduced F- anion and no reducible transition metal, so it should resist oxidation at 4 V vs Li. Its Li-F bonding is far more stable than the La-containing products (LaPO4, LaTaO4, LaNbO4, La2Zr2O7) that set the LLZO contact penalties for all oxide and phosphate candidates so far. It is a different chemical family from every tested candidate, so it tests whether a halide interface avoids the La-oxide reactions.
proposals.motivation: Every oxide and phosphate tested (Li3PO4, Li2ZrO3, LiTaO3, LiAlO2, Li3BO3, LiNbO3, Li3TaO4, Li2TiO3, LiZr2(PO4)3) gave contact penalties of 0.02 to 0.31 driven by La-containing products, and none had both penalties below threshold. A fluoride is an unexplored family that may avoid these reactions.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with both the Li-rich LLZO garnet and LiCoO2. Its PO4 framework should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li and form a low-reactivity interface, so it is a strong first test for a coating that blocks electron transfer while passing Li ions.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap lithium zirconate that shares Zr with the LLZO garnet, so it should avoid the La-phosphate and ZrO2 decomposition seen for Li3PO4 at the electrolyte contact. It is also a known LiCoO2 coating chemistry, and its Li-rich oxide framework should be electrochemically stable near 4 V with low electronic conductivity.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 was insulating with a wide gap but had a contact penalty of 0.099 eV/atom (bin 4, above the 0.05 threshold), driven by reaction with LLZO to LaPO4, O2 and ZrO2. A coating that avoids phosphate and matches the garnet's Zr chemistry should reduce that reactive penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiTaO3 is a wide-gap, d0 Ta5+ perovskite-type oxide that is a known LiCoO2 coating chemistry. Its Ta5+ should resist reduction by the Li-rich LLZO garnet better than Li2ZrO3 decomposes, and it avoids the phosphate-to-LaPO4 pathway that gave Li3PO4 a 0.099 eV/atom contact penalty. The aim is a lower self-decomposition penalty than Li2ZrO3 (0.30) with an acceptable contact reaction.
